=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: line 2365 (RETRY_ACTIVE_RUN selection logic)
  Problem: The workflow run list discovery uses per_page=100 and then selects the oldest run from that subset using `sort_by(.created_at, .id) | .[0]`.
  Why it fails at runtime: On branches with high turnover (e.g., long-lived smoke branches), there may be more than 100 historical runs. If the truly oldest active matching run exists outside the most recent 100, the script will fail to adopt it and instead dispatch a redundant new run, failing to achieve the intended concurrency reduction.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 2330-2334
  Problem: The script now explicitly exits with `retry_dispatch_failed` if the workflow run list discovery fails.
  Why it fails at runtime: This is a regression; the previous implementation did not gate the retry logic on a successful listing. A transient GitHub API error during listing will now hard-fail the release gate verification even if a dispatch would have succeeded.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 2317 (RETRY_DISPATCH_SHA capture) and 2462 (poll filter)
  Problem: RETRY_DISPATCH_SHA is captured before dispatch, but the post-dispatch registration filter (line 2462) rejects any run whose head_sha is not BAIT_SHA or RETRY_DISPATCH_SHA.
  Why it fails at runtime: If the branch advances (e.g., due to a concurrent sync or commit) between the initial capture and the poll filter execution, the new workflow run's head_sha will not match the stale captured SHA. This causes the filter to reject all candidates, leading to `retry_dispatch_failed` even though the run was successfully dispatched.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: line ~2317 (RETRY_DISPATCH_SHA capture), line ~2381 (gh workflow run dispatch), line ~2462 (registration polling filter)
  Problem: RETRY_DISPATCH_SHA is captured before the new dispatch and then used in the registration polling's `head_sha == $bait_sha or .head_sha == $retry_sha` filter. If the branch advances between capture and the 90-second registration window expiring (e.g. a sync merge or another push lands during the window), the newly dispatched run's head_sha will be neither BAIT_SHA nor RETRY_DISPATCH_SHA — the filter rejects every candidate, the registration deadline trips, and the step exits with `status=retry_dispatch_failed`.
  Why it fails at runtime: Edge case during the 90-second registration window. The original code had the same staleness concern (filter by RETRY_DISPATCH_SHA only). retry_dispatch_failed is reached only when a branch advance lands within 90s of dispatch — low probability, but a regression relative to the intent of polling exact run IDs.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml
  Line or code reference: lines 2317, 2381, 2462 — RETRY_DISPATCH_SHA captured before dispatch, then used to filter post-dispatch registration
  Problem: RETRY_DISPATCH_SHA is snapshotted at line 2317 before the runs listing and dispatch. The post-dispatch registration filter at line 2462 selects runs where head_sha matches BAIT_SHA or RETRY_DISPATCH_SHA. If the branch advances between the snapshot and the gh workflow run dispatch (e.g., a sync merge lands during the discovery phase), the newly dispatched run's head_sha will be the newer branch tip, which matches neither filter value. The 90-second registration window then expires with no matching run and the step exits retry_dispatch_failed.
  Why it fails at runtime: The branch-advance race is narrow but real on the stable branch where forward-merge and promote jobs run concurrently. The old code did not pre-filter on a snapshotted SHA, so it was immune to this specific race. Mitigation would be to also accept the live branch head at registration time, or to re-resolve the head after dispatch.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
